AN IMPORTANT MATTER

The European elite arrives at Enbesa in search of a new paradise, one that promises sun, wealth and exoticism all year round.
The distinguished delegation made up of the self-proclaimed Sybarites has landed on the Enbesan coast, ready to strengthen cultural ties and strengthen relationships between nations.
This opportunity presents new challenges but also opportunities to open new trade routes and obtain new markets for the import and export of exclusive goods.
Enbesa welcomes its new citizens, who bring the best of European culture and customs to the wild lands.

The Queen
Clara Méndez, Creator of Reusable Filters

A meticulous Colombian engineer, Clara dedicated her career to perfecting drip coffee makers, transforming them into precision instruments. Her reusable filters accurately regulate water flow, extracting a more intense and consistent flavor with every brew.
Anthony Westwick, Exotic Herbal Tea Sommelier

Westwick traveled to distant ports and markets cataloging leaves, peels, and fruits destined for infusion. He learned to distinguish an ordinary fruit from one with worthy potential with the same precision with which others judge a wine. That experience led him to treat fruit tea as a beverage to be tasted.
Silvano Palmetti, Botanist who discovered the Golden Palm

During an expedition to remote archipelagos in Ecuador, Palmetti identified a unique variety of palm whose leaves shone as if they held gold in their sap. From then on, he dedicated his work and life to reproducing and adapting that species for productive plantations.
Eleanor Schaffer, Dressmaker Specializing in Gloves

Schaffer transformed the humble glove into a luxury item, where every seam serves both an aesthetic and a practical purpose. In his workshops, the leather is selected for its softness and durability before being shaped into pieces that move with the hand without hindering it.

Orleans dedicated his career to studying how the finest fibers could withstand the demands of modern production without losing quality or strength. Thanks to his methods, once fragile fabrics became reliable materials for industrial garment manufacturing.
Fiodora Verdelli, Milliner of the Tropics

With prodigious skill, Fidora transforms humble palm leaves into hats so elegant that even the tropics seem to bow before them. In her workshops, each frond is selected and shaped with precision, combining aesthetics and strength, so that each piece is both durable and refined.

Known for their impressive size, Chinook salmon eggs were fundamental to both commercial fishing and early farming experiments in the early 20th century. Their presence marked a milestone in the fishing economy and laid the foundation for modern aquaculture.
Dr. Magnus Torsk, Zoologist and Salmon Farmer

A pioneer in controlled salmon farming, Dr. Torsk perfected the use of salmon farms to ensure healthier and more abundant salmon year-round. His work transformed traditional fishing into a planned industry, where science and patience replace the unpredictable nature of the sea.

The undisputed king of lunch, Doyle has mastered the art of layering flavors and textures in precise ways that transform the everyday into the extraordinary. Whether it's a simple sandwich or a gourmet shrimp dish, every ingredient occupies a calculated place within a perfectly edible structure.
Don Tocornal, Inspector of Social Sobriety

A legendary figure in the salons of Valparaíso and Santiago, Don Tocornal learned among vineyards and taverns that the true art of wine lies not in drinking more, but in drinking better. He frequents bars, brothels, and restaurants like a discreet gentleman, fine-tuning recipes until excess becomes refined conviviality.
Aurelio Montreval, Genius of Modern Spectacle

A former entrepreneur of art fairs and theaters, Montreval understood before anyone else that the elite seek not just stories, but complete experiences. He transformed the nascent cinema and theater into temples of wonder, where lights, music, and stage machinery work in unison to keep the audience captivated.
Silvestre Montbard, High Commissioner for Civil Attraction

A veteran of countless treaties and official receptions, from the consulate's halls he orchestrates prestige campaigns, promises of stability, and favorable agreements that attract new sybarites like moths to a flame. His pen transforms taxes into acceptable compromises and migration into social investment.
Héctor Valdemar Quintray, General Supervisor of Urban Services

Trained in public works offices and social planning rooms, Quintray maintains that luxury is only possible when the infrastructure functions flawlessly. He has dedicated his career to coordinating urban infrastructure as if it were parts of a single, perfectly oiled machine.
Octavio Bellamy, Regulator of Urban Lifestyle

Convinced that prosperity is built on well-directed habits, Bellamy transformed affluent, progressive districts into models of elegant and rational consumption. His standards for procurement and domestic organization allow for reduced consumption without diminishing the everyday experience.
Sigrún Nýhlfjörð, Supervisor of Refined Manufacturing

Trained in industrial workshops and in the north, Sigrún applied industrial discipline to the world of high-end luxury goods. Her talent lies in improving production, making factories operate with clockwork precision regardless of the additional costs involved.

A compendium of meticulously compiled research that organizes and preserves the latest advances in scientific thought. Its pages transform isolated observations into verifiable and accessible knowledge for scholars worldwide.

A letter arriving from distant lands, carrying words brimming with affection and shared memories. Reading it eases the distance and transforms the wait into companionship, easing the nostalgia inherent in long-distance communication.

Few things brighten the day more than a child's heartfelt words, written with affection and endearing awkwardness. Every line conveys closeness, even from the greatest distance. Reading them makes any other correspondence seem superfluous compared to that irreplaceable bond.

A mother's words carry a warmth and tenderness that no other message can match. In every sentence, you can feel the care, concern, and constant love that transcends distance. Reading them comforts the soul and brings back a sense of home, even in the most distant places.
Beatrice Van Holtz, Curator of Aristocratic Wellbeing

A specialist in the domestic life of high society, Van Holtz learned that even luxury needs rules to avoid becoming excessive. She reformed the management of investor mansions through service protocols, moderate consumption, and the efficient distribution of comfort.
Marguerite Delacroix, Administrator of Domestic Welfare

Convinced that luxury begins with everyday order, Delacroix dedicates her career to optimizing life in the first gourmet neighborhoods. It introduced domestic routines, efficient distribution of provisions, and norms of coexistence that reduce waste without sacrificing comfort.
Nahla Yafouri, Guardian of the Jaffa's Oranges

Forced to leave her home among the orange groves of Jaffa, Nahla set off for South America with a few seeds hidden among her belongings. There, in the land that offered her a new beginning, she planted the seeds of the land that saw her birth, for as long as she live, the oranges of Jaffa will grow.

Trained in the most demanding kitchens of the European continent, Beaumont was sent to Enbesa to adapt haute cuisine to distant ingredients and climates. There she learned to combine refined techniques with local spices, transforming restaurants into showcases of culinary prestige.
Vittoria Sambuco, Empress of Aromatic Stills

Descended from an ancient house of Italian royalty and heir to a lineage of master distillers, Vittoria learned to mix nobility and craft in the same glass. In its stills, courtly protocols and recipes transmitted in low voices for generations are combined.
Leopold von Edelstein, Rare Gem Trader

A descendant of an old family of Prussian imperial gemologists, he has dedicated his life to the search for and trade of the rarest and most precious stones. His contacts extend from forgotten mines and black markets to aristocratic salons where every gem tells a story.
